introduction: Follow Goortok’s tests and the blind monk’s requests through the caves and beyond. Each accepted return has its own journal card. Their dialogue suggests an order, but the returns are accepted independently. Discovery is separate. New progress requires active, ready accounting.
orientation: ASK GOORTOK about moralon to learn about the mountain’s name. His tests ask for a silver disc, a platinum disc and a strange vial. Each offering is accepted on its own and gives a response rather than an item or coin reward. Hearing an answer does not complete an offering.

The silver disc is declared inside a skeletal corpse in the deep cave beyond the trapper. The exact platinum disc and strange vial have prototypes, but this source review found no active declared producer for either. Existing matching supplied items can fit. Similar names and other discs or vials cannot substitute.

The Moralon clue appears in a tree inscription in the northern wilderness and in golden-flecked cave writing that points toward a Calim desert oasis. Goortok’s final test asks you to find a name on an ancient monolith. Follow the inscriptions for the answer. Hearing his response and learning the name remain separate from accepted offering history.

Goortok carries the stone key for the locked downward passage beside him. The boulder approach is an ordinary closed door in the current world. Key possession, unlocking, opening and passage differ, and existing shared access can change which keys you need.

The blind monk is declared at the mountain top. ASK MONK about greetings, solace, tyrrany, eyes, help, task or glass for his native leads and aliases. The large rock on the mountain path is the declared travel object, but its configured verb differs from the current climb command. Ordinary access needs builder qualification; climbing skill alone is not proof of arriving at the monk.

The monk accepts the goblin king’s bronze scepter together with the orc chief’s engraved bracelet for a copper mask. He separately accepts the flaming shield from the warlord of fire for frozen leggings. The first pair requires both exact items loose together; defeating the leaders is not a separate journal prerequisite. The suggested task sequence is tribal leaders, pyrohydra, warlord, then troll king; the game accepts each return independently.

The false marble eye is declared inside a stone desk in Pine Hollow, where opening the locked, pickable desk has a room-wide acid trap. The glass eye is declared inside the pile of skulls in the elven tomb. The monk accepts each eye independently for coins. These artificial eyes fill the monk’s empty sockets and improve his appearance; the native responses do not promise restored vision or persist that cosmetic change.

The pyrohydra declares both a polished silver bracelet and an amber bracelet. Bring that exact pair loose together for the monk’s ogrebone armplates. The nearby cryohydra is hazard context and does not replace either bracelet or create another accepted return.

The troll king declares the crystal sphere in the swamp. The monk accepts it for a trollhide belt and then departs. That return can be accepted before his other requests, so complete the returns you want while he is available. Departure and narrated liberation do not prove that all tyrants were defeated or the settlement was rescued.

These nine accepted returns preserve nine achievements and nine potential dailies under the current reset classification. Material rows show current loose inventory; accepted history survives after items are spent. Matching supplied stock is valid, without first recovery or personal kill proof. Daily eligibility and reset timing do not guarantee fresh items: new reset issuance is gated while accounting is active. New discovery, encounters and progress require active, ready accounting.

contacts.name: the orc chief
contacts.description: The orc chief declares the engraved bracelet for one of the monk’s paired returns. Encountering the source does not reveal or complete the monk’s requests.

contacts.name: the goblin king
contacts.description: The goblin king declares the bronze scepter. Defeat, recovery and the monk’s accepted pair are separate evidence.

contacts.name: a piercer
contacts.description: The local piercer is cave hazard context. Its ordinary encounter adds no accepted return or inferred ambush milestone.

contacts.name: Goortok
contacts.description: Goortok accepts three independent rewardless offerings and answers Moralon. His final test points toward the name written on an ancient monolith; discovering that answer is a separate lore lead.

contacts.name: a large trapper
contacts.description: The trapper is nearby cave danger on the silver-disc lead. Its defeat is not required for the accepted disc return.

contacts.name: a nine-headed pyrohydra
contacts.description: The pyrohydra declares the exact silver and amber bracelet pair. Encounter and material recovery are distinct from the monk’s acceptance.

contacts.name: a seven-headed cryohydra
contacts.description: The cryohydra is adjacent hazard context, without another accepted request or substitute for the pyrohydra’s bracelets.

contacts.name: a blind monk
contacts.description: The blind monk accepts six independent returns. His sphere reward makes him depart. His dialogue order, sight and liberation are narration without separate persisted milestones.
